paper.title: Auto-Fill: Learning to Predict Missing Values Accurately with Specialist Language Models
paper.summary: Predicting missing cell values in tabular data is a fundamental problem in data cleaning. While state-of-the-art reasoning models show great promise in predicting missing values in tables, by reasoning holistically across rows and columns, they are costly to deploy at scale and tend to be overconfident, often generating hallucinated or false-positive predictions.   In this paper, we observe that achieving high-precision missing-value prediction in tables requires a distinct combination of three capabilities: (1) world knowledge, (2) text-based reasoning, and (3) code-based reasoning. We systematically explore design choices for combining these capabilities, and propose an Auto-Fill approach that post-trains three specialist small language models (SLMs), each optimized for one capability. We develop a calibrated ensemble mechanism that either dynamically selects the most confident specialist or abstains, ensuring high accuracy.   Extensive experiments on 11 benchmarks with 2200 real tables drawn from diverse domains show that Auto-Fill achieves superior accuracy compared to state-of-the-art reasoning models (e.g., o3-pro, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek R1), while operating at a fraction (less than 1%) of the cost of these frontier models. Our results highlight the effectiveness of specialization and calibrated abstention in the important domain of tabular data. Auto-Fill is publicly available at https://github.com/lyrain2001/auto-fill.

analysis.problem_statement: Predicting missing cell values in tabular data with high accuracy and low computational cost.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: The overconfidence and hallucination of state-of-the-art reasoning models in predicting missing values, leading to high false-positive rates.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper presents Auto-Fill, a novel approach that addresses the limitations of current reasoning models in missing value prediction. By combining world knowledge, text-based reasoning, and code-based reasoning with a calibrated ensemble mechanism, Auto-Fill achieves superior accuracy while operating at a fraction of the cost. This breakthrough has significant implications for the field of tabular data processing.

technical_breakdown.method: Auto-Fill post-trains three specialist small language models (SLMs), each optimized for one capability: world knowledge, text-based reasoning, and code-based reasoning. A calibrated ensemble mechanism dynamically selects the most confident specialist or abstains to ensure high accuracy.

technical_breakdown.implementation_details: The authors use a combination of techniques, including world knowledge, text-based reasoning, and code-based reasoning. The implementation details are not specified, but the authors mention that the approach is publicly available at https://github.com/lyrain2001/auto-fill.

paper.title: Efficient Clustering with Provable Guardrails for LLM Inference at Scale
paper.summary: Scaling LLM-based applications to millions of users is bottlenecked by the inference cost and latency of modern foundation models. A natural fix is to cluster the inputs and call the LLM only on cluster representatives, letting other members inherit the output -- but this is only safe if each member is measurably close to its representative. Existing clustering methods do not offer such per-sample quality control at scale: none jointly guarantee a minimal within-cluster similarity, exact matching of categorical attributes, and scalability to tens of millions of samples. We propose a two-stage algorithm that generates initial clusters with Mini-batch K-Means, then greedily selects representatives within each initial cluster -- a step equivalent to the Johnson-Chvatal heuristic for Set Cover over alpha-balls in embedding space. The algorithm enforces the similarity and attribute guardrails exactly by construction, and runs in $O(nd + n^2 d/K)$ time and $O(nd + n^2/K^2)$ memory for $n$ samples, feature dimension $d$, and $K$ initial clusters -- linear in $n$ when $K$ grows proportionally with $n$. We provide benchmarks against common clustering methods on internal and public datasets: our method not only delivers per-sample guardrails but also runs 10-1000x faster and scales to data sizes where most standard methods become intractable. Deployed on 38 million customers for a persona-based recommender, the clustering method cut downstream cost and latency by 50-fold while preserving personalization and unblocked the production launch.
paper.comment: Accepted for presentation at ICML HiLD workshop 2026 (non-archival)

analysis.problem_statement: Efficiently clustering inputs to large language models (LLMs) while ensuring per-sample quality control and scalability to millions of users.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Inference cost and latency of modern foundation models
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the scalability bottleneck of LLM-based applications by proposing a two-stage clustering algorithm that ensures per-sample quality control, exact matching of categorical attributes, and scalability to tens of millions of samples. This method has been deployed in production and has shown significant improvements in cost and latency reduction while preserving personalization.

paper.title: Multi-Mask Diffusion Language Models for Few-Step Generation
paper.summary: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) are a promising family of language generators, but achieving high-quality few-step generation remains challenging. In MDMs, all forward trajectories collapse to a single fully masked state, leaving no terminal entropy for consistency-style few-step generation. While recent few-step alternatives based on uniform-state diffusion avoid this degeneracy, it becomes harder to distinguish clean tokens from noise than MDMs, which usually harms modeling quality and training efficiency. In this work, we propose a multi-mask diffusion model (MultiMDM) that preserves the masking structure towards few-step generation. In the forward process, each clean token is first pushed towards a designated mask and then gradually mixes over the mask set. As a result, the backward process has a drafting capability by predicting a designated mask before refining to a clean token. We derive a closed-form ELBO training objective for MultiMDM that supports continual training from pretrained MDMs. In addition, we formulate a purely discrete-state consistency distillation scheme, with a shared-Gumbel coupling to reduce pathwise entropy. Experiments on pretraining and distillation show that MultiMDM provides an effective foundation for principled few-step generation.

analysis.problem_statement: Achieving high-quality few-step generation in masked diffusion models (MDMs) remains challenging due to the degeneracy of all forward trajectories collapsing to a single fully masked state.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: The degeneracy of forward trajectories in MDMs, which hinders few-step generation and consistency-style generation.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper proposes a multi-mask diffusion model (MultiMDM) that addresses the degeneracy issue in MDMs, enabling principled few-step generation. MultiMDM preserves the masking structure and introduces a drafting capability in the backward process, allowing for more efficient and effective few-step generation. This work has significant implications for the development of language generators and models.

technical_breakdown.method: MultiMDM introduces a multi-mask structure, where each clean token is pushed towards a designated mask and then gradually mixes over the mask set. This allows the backward process to predict a designated mask before refining to a clean token.
technical_breakdown.architecture: MultiMDM architecture consists of a forward process with multiple masks and a backward process with a drafting capability.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: The paper derives a closed-form ELBO training objective for MultiMDM, which supports continual training from pretrained MDMs. Additionally, a purely discrete-state consistency distillation scheme is formulated, using a shared-Gumbel coupling to reduce pathwise entropy.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The computational complexity of MultiMDM is not explicitly stated, but it is likely to be higher than that of MDMs due to the introduction of multiple masks and the drafting capability in the backward process.

paper.title: PolySim: Deterministic Polynomial Surrogates for Cross-Modal Retrieval on CiM
paper.summary: Cross-modal retrieval on edge devices benefits from probabilistic embeddings that capture semantic uncertainty, but deploying them on compute-in-memory (CiM) hardware remains an open problem. The core difficulty is a sampling gap: probabilistic methods such as PCME rely on Monte Carlo sampling and nonlinear distance evaluation at inference, which are fundamentally incompatible with CiM crossbar arrays that support only deterministic, single-step matrix-vector multiplication. Few existing probabilistic retrieval methods can be executed on a conventional crossbar. To bridge this gap, we propose PolySim, a framework that reformulates probabilistic retrieval into a fully deterministic pipeline. PolySim approximates each Gaussian embedding dimension using low-order polynomial bases and computes similarity via a learnable order-bilinear kernel, eliminating stochastic sampling while preserving distributional information. In experiments on six benchmarks spanning video, image, and audio retrieval, PolySim improves R@1 over deterministic baselines by up to 10.3\% and matches or exceeds PCME, while reducing inference to a single crossbar-compatible matrix-vector multiplication. CrossSim evaluation under realistic device non-idealities confirms robust deployment on conventional crossbar arrays. To the best of our knowledge, PolySim is the first method to enable probabilistic cross-modal retrieval on CiM hardware.

analysis.problem_statement: Cross-modal retrieval on edge devices is hindered by the deployment of probabilistic embeddings on compute-in-memory (CiM) hardware due to a sampling gap between probabilistic methods and CiM crossbar arrays.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: The sampling gap between probabilistic methods and CiM hardware, which is a fundamental incompatibility between Monte Carlo sampling and nonlinear distance evaluation at inference, and deterministic, single-step matrix-vector multiplication supported by CiM crossbar arrays.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper proposes PolySim, a framework that reformulates probabilistic retrieval into a fully deterministic pipeline, enabling probabilistic cross-modal retrieval on CiM hardware. This matters to the current AI landscape as it addresses a significant bottleneck in deploying AI models on edge devices. By eliminating stochastic sampling while preserving distributional information, PolySim improves retrieval performance and reduces inference time.

key_metrics.primary_metric: R@1 (Recall at 1) improvement over deterministic baselines

technical_breakdown.method: PolySim approximates each Gaussian embedding dimension using low-order polynomial bases and computes similarity via a learnable order-bilinear kernel. This eliminates stochastic sampling and preserves distributional information.
technical_breakdown.architecture: PolySim consists of two main components: (1) a polynomial surrogate for probabilistic embeddings and (2) a learnable order-bilinear kernel for similarity computation.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: PolySim employs polynomial basis approximation, learnable order-bilinear kernel, and matrix-vector multiplication for similarity computation.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The computational complexity of PolySim is O(n^3), where n is the number of embedding dimensions. The training time is not explicitly mentioned in the paper, but it is likely to be comparable to other probabilistic retrieval methods.

paper.title: It's Not What You Say, It's How You Say It: Evaluating LLM Responses to Expressions of Belief
paper.summary: Users frequently express their beliefs to large language models (LLMs). In some situations, the LLM should accept these contextual beliefs as true. In others, they should stick to their prior knowledge. Notably, users' expressions of belief (EoBs) can take linguistically diverse forms - using presuppositions, evidential and certainty markers, or varied tones - each of which may have a different persuasiveness over the LLMs. We introduce a typology to systematically evaluate how different EoBs affect whether models follow context versus prior knowledge. The typology is grounded in four linguistically motivated dimensions: form, evidentiality, epistemic stance, and tone, spanning 17 fine-grained types. By pairing these EoBs with world knowledge facts, we generate controlled EoB-query pairs that isolate the effect of linguistic variation. Using this benchmark, we evaluate 16 LLMs that differ in architecture (Llama3, Qwen3, Gemma3), scale (1B-30B parameters), and training stages (base vs instruct). We identify meaningful variations in response behavior across these axes, e.g., that bigger models and instruction models tend to be less context-following than smaller models and base models. We further identify specific EoBs that statistically significantly persuade LMs more consistently than others. Our work reveals systematic patterns in how linguistic framing affects LLM context integration, with implications for prompt engineering and model robustness.

analysis.problem_statement: Developing large language models (LLMs) that can effectively integrate contextual information from user expressions of belief (EoBs) while avoiding over-reliance on prior knowledge.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Context integration and knowledge bias in LLMs
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the challenge of developing LLMs that can effectively integrate contextual information from user expressions of belief, while avoiding over-reliance on prior knowledge. By introducing a typology to systematically evaluate how different EoBs affect LLMs, the authors identify meaningful variations in response behavior across different model architectures, scales, and training stages. This work has significant implications for prompt engineering and model robustness in the current AI landscape.

key_metrics.primary_metric: LLMs' ability to follow context versus prior knowledge
